m.desc: The physical unit "m" is a meter, a base unit of length in the International System of Units (SI). It is commonly used to measure distances and sizes in various fields of science and everyday life.

g.desc: The unit "g" is a metric unit of mass, also known as gram. It is the base unit for measuring mass and is commonly used in scientific and everyday applications.

s.desc: The physical unit "s" is a time measurement known as a second. It is a base unit of time. It is commonly used in various fields for measuring durations and intervals.

a.desc: "A" is the unit of electric current, symbolized as ampere and is a base unit. It measures the flow of electric charge in a circuit.

k.desc: The Kelvin (K) is the base unit of temperature in the International System of Units (SI). It is commonly used in scientific and engineering applications, where 0K represents absolute zero.

mol.desc: The mole (mol) is the base unit for amount of substance in the International System of Units (SI). It represents a specific number of entities, such as atoms or molecules, in a sample.

cd.desc: The candela (cd) is the SI unit for luminous intensity, measuring the amount of light emitted by a source in a particular direction.

rad.desc: The radian (rad) is a unit of measurement for plane angles, equivalent to the angle subtended at the center of a circle by an arc equal in length to the radius.

sr.desc: The steradian (sr) is the SI unit for measuring solid angles.

usd.desc: "USD" is a currency unit known as the US dollar. It is the base unit for monetary transactions in the United States and is widely used internationally.

abcoulomb.desc: The abcoulomb is a unit of electric charge, equivalent to 10^6 coulombs. It is used to measure large amounts of charge in electrical systems.

coulomb.desc: The coulomb is the SI unit of electric charge, representing the amount of charge passing a point in a circuit per second when a current of one ampere is flowing.

fdy.desc: "fdy" is a unit of electric charge and represents a specific amount of charge.

fr.desc: The physical unit "fr" is a unit of electric charge. It is used to measure the amount of charge present in a system.

abfarad.desc: The abfarad is a unit of capacitance in the CGS system, equal to 10^9 farads. It is rarely used in modern scientific contexts due to its large value.

statfarad.desc: The statfarad is a unit of capacitance in the electrostatic cgs system, equivalent to 1.11265 x 10^-12 farads. It is used to measure small capacitance values.

abhenry.desc: The abhenry is a unit of inductance in the CGS system, equivalent to 10^-9 henries. It is used to measure the ability of a circuit to store energy in a magnetic field.

hy.desc: The unit "hy" is a measure of inductance in the International System of Units. It represents the amount of inductance in a circuit.

stathenry.desc: The stathenry is a unit of inductance in the electrostatic cgs system, equal to 1 statvolt per ampere. It is rarely used in modern applications.

abmho.desc: The abmho is a unit of electrical conductance, representing the reciprocal of an ohm in the CGS electromagnetic unit system. It is denoted by the symbol abmho.

mho.desc: The "mho" is a unit of electrical conductance, equal to one reciprocal ohm. It is also known as the siemens in the International System of Units (SI).

statmho.desc: The statmho is a unit of electrical conductance in the CGS system, equivalent to 1/(8.9875 x 10^11) siemens. It is commonly used in electrostatics and related fields.

abohm.desc: The abohm is a unit of electrical impedance, equivalent to 10^-9 ohms. It is used to measure the resistance to the flow of alternating current in a circuit.

statohm.desc: The statohm is a unit of electrical resistance in the electrostatic cgs system. It is equivalent to 8.9875 x 10^11 ohms and is used to measure impedance in high-frequency circuits.

abvolt.desc: The abvolt is a unit of electric potential in the CGS system, equal to 10^-8 volts. It is used to measure small electrical potentials in scientific research and engineering.

statvolt.desc: Statvolt is a unit of electric potential in the cgs electrostatic system of units. It is equivalent to 299.8 volts in the SI system.

ci.desc: The "ci" unit is used to measure frequency or heart rate.

rpm.desc: "RPM" stands for rotations per minute, a unit of angular velocity measuring the number of complete rotations an object makes in one minute. It is commonly used in machinery and automotive industries.

clo.desc: The "clo" is a unit of thermal resistance coefficient used to measure the insulation level of clothing. It indicates the amount of insulation provided by a garment.

cp.desc: The unit "cp" is used to measure dynamic fluid viscosity. It is commonly known as centipoise. It quantifies a fluid's resistance to flow.

p.desc: The physical unit "p" represents dynamic fluid viscosity. It is used to measure the resistance of a fluid to flow.

cst.desc: The unit "cst" is a measure of viscosity, specifically centistokes, representing the rate of flow of a fluid.

stk.desc: "stk" is a unit of measurement of viscosity. It is commonly used to quantify viscosity in various substances.

fc.desc: The unit "fc" is used to measure illuminance, representing the amount of light falling on a surface.

ph.desc: The "ph" unit is a measurement of illuminance, representing the quantity of light per unit area.

flam.desc: The flam is a unit of luminance, representing the amount of light emitted or reflected from a surface.

gama.desc: "Gama" is a unit of measurement for magnetic flux density, denoted as γ. It is equivalent to one nanotesla (1 nT) and is commonly used in the field of magnetism and electromagnetism."

gs.desc: The unit "gs" is a measurement of magnetic flux density, representing gauss. It is defined as 1 gram per second squared per ampere.

ky.desc: The unit "ky" is a wavenumber unit used in optics to represent the spatial frequency along the y-axis. It is dimensionally reciprocal to length (L-1).

lambert.desc: A lambert is a unit of luminance, representing brightness emitted or reflected by a surface. It is equivalent to one candela per square centimeter.

langley.desc: A langley is a unit used to measure solar radiation or energy received on a unit area over a certain time period. It is commonly used in the study of surface tension and spectral irradiance in physics.

mpg.desc: "MPG", or miles per gallon, is a unit of measurement used to determine the fuel efficiency of a vehicle. It represents the distance in miles a vehicle can travel on one gallon of fuel.

mx.desc: The "mx" is a unit used to measure magnetic flux. It is typically used in the field of magnetism and electromagnetism.

oe.desc: The physical unit "oe" is used to measure magnetic field strength or magnetization. It is commonly known as oersted (oe).

r.desc: "r" is a unit of measurement. (review pending)

radu.desc: The "radu" is a unit of measurement for specific energy and radioactive dose. It is commonly used in the field of radiation and represents a measure of radiation exposure.

rem.desc: "Rem" is a unit of measurement for absorbed dose of ionizing radiation, taking into account the biological effects of different types of radiation on human tissue.

sb.desc: The unit "sb" is a measure of luminance, representing the amount of light emitted or reflected from a surface. It is commonly known as steradian per square meter.

sphere.desc: A sphere is a three-dimensional geometric shape that is perfectly round and symmetrical, with all points equidistant from the center. It is a unit of measurement in solid angle

st.desc: The "st" (steradian) is the SI unit of solid angle, representing the extent of a cone's surface that intersects a sphere at its center. It measures spatial coverage in 3D space.

te.desc: The physical unit "te" is a unit of magnetic flux density. It is commonly used to measure the strength of magnetic fields in various applications.

unc.desc: "unc" is a virtual unit of currency used in qCalc to represent User's National Currency (UNC). Can be used in calculations where actual currency and exchange rate is irrelevant.

upole.desc: The upole is a unit of magnetic flux. It is known as upole and is used to measure magnetic field strength in certain applications.

unit.desc: A "unit" is a dimensionless quantity representing a single entity or item. It is a standard reference for comparison or measurement in various fields.

beat.desc: A beat is a unitless measure of a single contraction and relaxation of the heart muscle, known as a heartbeat. It is a common way to measure heart rate and rhythm.

bag.desc: A bag is a unitless physical quantity used to measure the amount of something that can fit inside a bag. It is often used to measure bulk items such as grains, produce, cement or other goods.

bale.desc: A bale is a unitless measure used to describe a compressed bundle of material, typically used for packaging or shipping goods such as hay, cotton, or paper products.

bundle.desc: A bundle is a unitless physical quantity typically used to group items together for sale or transport.

dozen.desc: A dozen is a unit of quantity that represents 12 items. It is commonly used to refer to a group of twelve things, such as eggs, donuts, or roses.

ea.desc: "ea" is a unitless quantity used to represent individual items or objects. It stands for "each". It is commonly used in retail and inventory management.

hali.desc: "Hali" is a unitless physical quantity. It is known as a "four piece" and is used in various contexts to represent a set or group of four items or components.

hd.desc: The unit "hd" stands for hundred and is a unitless measure. It is commonly used to represent a quantity of one hundred items or units.

myria.desc: A myria is a unitless quantity. (review pending)

person.desc: A person is a unitless entity representing an individual human being. It is used as a reference for measurements and calculations in various fields such as demographics and statistics.

nos.desc: "Nos" is a unitless quantity used to represent numbers or countable items. It is commonly referred to as "numbers."

pair.desc: A "pair" is a unitless quantity representing a set of two items or objects. It is used to denote a quantity of two items that are often considered together as a single entity.

pct.desc: The physical unit "pct" is a unitless measurement representing a percentage, denoting a proportion out of 100. It is commonly used to express relative quantities or values.

ppm.desc: "ppm" stands for parts per million, a unitless measurement used to express the concentration of a substance in a mixture. It signifies one part in a million parts.

quire.desc: A quire is a unitless measure traditionally used in bookbinding and papermaking, consisting of 24 sheets of paper or parchment folded to create 48 pages.

ream.desc: A ream is a unit of paper quantity equal to 500 sheets. It is commonly used in the paper industry for measuring and packaging paper products.

kg.desc: The kilogram (kg) is the base unit of mass in the International System of Units (SI). It is equal to the mass of the international prototype of the kilogram, a platinum-iridium cylinder stored at the International Bureau of Weights and Measures in France.

hz.desc: "Hertz" (Hz) is a unit of frequency measuring cycles per second. Commonly used to describe the frequency of waves, it is a key unit in physics and engineering.

bpm.desc: "BPM" stands for beats per minute, a unit used to measure the frequency of events, particularly heart rate. It signifies the number of beats in a one-minute time frame.

bph.desc: "BPH" stands for beats per hour, a unit used to measure frequency or heart rate. It represents the number of beats occurring in one hour.

n.desc: The newton (symbol: N) is a unit of force in the International System of Units (SI). It is defined as the force required to accelerate a mass of one kilogram at a rate of one meter per second squared.

pa.desc: The pascal (Pa) is the SI unit of pressure, stress, energy density, and spectral exposure. It is defined as one newton per square meter.

j.desc: The physical unit "j" is a unit of energy. It is also known as the joule.

w.desc: The physical unit "w" is a measurement of power. It is commonly known as a watt and represents the rate at which energy is transferred or converted.

kw.desc: A kilowatt (kW) is a unit of power measuring 1000 watts. It is commonly used to quantify the rate at which energy is transferred or work is done in various applications.

mw.desc: A megawatt (MW) is a unit of power equal to one million watts. It is commonly used to measure the power output of large electrical generation plants or industrial equipment.

clm.desc: The "clm" is a unit of electric charge, also known as coulomb. It represents the amount of charge passing a point in one second.

v.desc: The unit "v" is the volt, a measure of electric potential. It represents the amount of potential energy required to move one coulomb of charge between two points in an electric circuit.

f.desc: The physical unit "f" is a unit of capacitance, representing the ability of a system to store electrical charge. It is commonly known as the farad.

ohm.desc: The ohm is a unit of electrical resistance in the International System of Units, represented by the symbol Ω. It is the amount of resistance that impedes the flow of current in a circuit.

si.desc: "Si" is the unit of electrical conductance in the International System of Units (SI), symbolized as "S". It is named after Ernst Werner von Siemens.

wb.desc: The weber (Wb) is the SI derived unit of magnetic flux. It measures the amount of magnetic flux that passes through a surface. It is equivalent to one volt-second.

ts.desc: The "ts" is a unit of measurement for magnetic flux density, also known as tesla. It is commonly used in the field of electromagnetism.

tesla.desc: The tesla is the unit of measurement for magnetic flux density. It is equivalent to one weber per square meter and is named after inventor Nikola Tesla.

hn.desc: The "hn" is a unit of inductance, also known as henry. It measures the amount of opposition to changes in current flow in a circuit.

lm.desc: The unit "lm" represents luminous flux or luminous power, measuring the total amount of visible light emitted by a source. It is commonly known as the lumen.

lx.desc: The unit "lx" is a measurement of illuminance, representing the amount of light that strikes a surface. It is equivalent to one lumen per square meter and is commonly known as lux.

bq.desc: The "bq" or becquerel is a unit of frequency measuring radioactive decay. It represents one decay per second. It is commonly used in nuclear physics and radiochemistry.

gy.desc: The gray (Gy) is a unit of ionizing radiation dose, measuring absorbed energy per unit mass. It is used in radiation therapy and radiation protection.

sv.desc: The sievert (sv) is a unit of radiation dose equivalent to one joule of energy deposited per kilogram of tissue. It measures the biological impact of ionizing radiation on living organisms.

hfcs.desc: "hfcs" is a unit of frequency representing the caesium hyperfine frequency, commonly used in measuring heart rate. It is a defining constant in the SI system.

c.desc: The physical unit "c" is a velocity unit. It represents the speed of light in a vacuum, a fundamental constant in physics.

hplanck.desc: The hplanck is a physical unit representing the Planck constant, denoted as h, used in quantum mechanics to quantify angular momentum and action. It is one of the seven SI defining constants.

hbar.desc: "hbar" is a physical unit representing the reduced Planck constant. It is used in quantum mechanics to quantify angular momentum, action, and spin.

ec.desc: The "ec" unit, known as electron charge, is a fundamental unit of electric charge in the SI system. It is the charge of a single electron and is the 4th of 7 defining constants in the SI system.

k_b.desc: The physical unit "k_b" is the Boltzmann constant, a fundamental constant in physics related to entropy and heat capacity. It is one of the seven SI defining constants.

nav.desc: The unit "nav" is a physical unit, representing the Avogadro constant. It is one of the 7 SI defining constants. (review pending)

kcd.desc: The "kcd" is a unit of luminous efficacy measuring the efficiency of visible radiation. It is the 7th of 7 SI defining constants.

mu0.desc: "mu0" is the permeability of vacuum, denoted as 4π x 10^-7 H/m. It measures the ability of vacuum to support magnetic fields.

eps0.desc: "eps0" is a physical unit representing the permittivity of vacuum. It is a fundamental constant in electromagnetism.

gv.desc: The physical unit "gv" is a unit of measurement, representing the gravitational constant. It is used to quantify the strength of the gravitational force between objects.

k_e.desc: The physical unit "k_e" is a constant in electromagnetism known as the coulomb constant. It is used in calculations involving electric fields.

cosmo.desc: The "cosmo" represents the cosmological constant. It is a dimensionless quantity denoting the energy density of empty space. (review pending)

sigma_sb.desc: The physical unit "sigma_sb" is the Stefan-Boltzmann constant, denoted as σ, with units of W/(m^2*K^4). It represents the energy radiated by a black body per unit surface area per unit time.

c1.desc: The physical unit "c1" is a constant known as the first radiation constant. It is used in various equations related to radiation and is a fundamental constant in physics. (review pending)

c1l.desc: The physical unit "c1l" is a constant used in the calculation of spectral radiance. It is known as the first radiation constant. (review pending)

c2.desc: The physical unit "c2" is a constant related to radiation. It is known as the second radiation constant. (review pending)

bw_wien.desc: The physical unit "bw_wien" is a constant related to Wien's displacement law, representing the peak wavelength of blackbody radiation. (review pending)

bf_wien.desc: The physical unit "bf_wien" is a constant used in Wien's frequency displacement law, representing the ratio of temperature to wavelength in the electromagnetic spectrum. (review pending)

be_wien.desc: The "be_wien" is a unit (review pending), representing the Wien entropy displacement law constant. It is used to quantify entropy displacement in terms of wavelength and temperature.

lplanck.desc: The Planck length, known as lplanck, is a theoretical unit of length in quantum mechanics, approximately equal to 1.61625518e-35 meters. It is the smallest possible length in the universe.

mplanck.desc: The "mplanck" is a unit of mass, known as the Planck mass. It is approximately 2.17643424e-8 kg, representing a tiny but fundamental mass scale in physics.

tplanck.desc: The "tplanck" is a unit of time known as the Planck time, approximately equal to 5.39124760e-44 seconds. It is used in physics for very short time intervals.

kplanck.desc: The kplanck is a unit of temperature, also known as the Planck temperature, representing the theoretical maximum temperature in the universe.

m_e.desc: The physical unit "m_e" represents the mass of an electron and is typically measured in kilograms. It is a fundamental constant in physics with a value of approximately 9.11 x 10^-31 kg.

m_mu.desc: The physical unit "m_mu" refers to the mass of a muon, a subatomic particle with a mass of approximately 105.7 mega-electronvolts/c^2. It is commonly used in particle physics research.

m_tau.desc: m_tau is a unit of mass, denoting the mass of the tau particle. It is commonly referred to as the tau mass.

m_p.desc: The physical unit "m_p" represents the mass of a proton, with a value of approximately 1.67 x 10^-27 kilograms. It is a fundamental constant in particle physics.

m_n.desc: The physical unit "m_n" is a unit of mass, representing the mass of a neutron. It is commonly referred to as the neutron mass.

m_tq.desc: The physical unit "m_tq" is a unit of mass, representing the top quark mass. It is commonly used in particle physics research.

mr_pe.desc: The physical unit "mr_pe" is a unitless quantity representing the proton to electron mass ratio, approximately equal to 1836.15267342. (review pending)

mu_b.desc: "mu_b" is a unit of magnetic moment, specifically magnetic dipole moment. It is also known as the Bohr magneton.

ryd.desc: The "ryd" is a unit of wavenumber or wavevector in the field of optical power. It is commonly known as the Rydberg constant in physics.

rg.desc: The physical unit "rg" is a molar gas constant. It is commonly used in thermodynamic calculations and has a value of approximately 8.314 J/(mol·K).

m_a.desc: The "m_a" physical unit is a measurement of mass in the field of atomic physics, specifically known as the atomic mass constant. It is denoted by the symbol "m_a". (review pending)

m_m.desc: The physical unit "m_m" is a unit used to represent molar mass constant.

fd.desc: The "fd" unit, also known as the Faraday constant, is a physical unit. It is commonly used in electrochemistry to represent the charge of one mole of electrons.

l_sun.desc: The physical unit "l_sun" is a measure of radiant flux or power, specifically the nominal solar luminosity. It represents the total power emitted by the Sun.

sigma_t.desc: Sigma_t is the total cross-sectional area for thomson scattering, representing the probability of interaction between a particle and incident radiation. (review pending)

l_bol0.desc: "l_bol0" is a unit of measurement of Power, representing the luminosity for absolute bolometric magnitude.

min.desc: The "min" is a unit of time commonly used to measure short durations. It is equal to 60 seconds or 1/60th of an hour. It is abbreviated as "min" and is known as a minute.

minute.desc: A minute is a unit of time equal to 60 seconds. It is commonly used for measuring short durations or intervals. Symbolized as min.

h.desc: The unit "h" is a time measurement equal to one hour. It is commonly used in various fields such as physics, astronomy, and everyday life for scheduling and timekeeping purposes.

hr.desc: "hr" is a unit of time, commonly known as hour. It is used to measure a period of 60 minutes or 1/24 of a day. It is commonly used in various fields such as scheduling, labor, and scientific measurements.

d.desc: The physical unit "d" represents a day, a unit of time equal to 24 hours. It is commonly used in various fields such as astronomy, economics, and scheduling.

day.desc: A day is a unit of time equal to 24 hours, typically used to measure the time it takes for the Earth to complete a full rotation on its axis. It is commonly divided into 24 hours, each hour consisting of 60 minutes.

sec.desc: The "sec" is a unit of time, symbolized as "s", commonly known as a second. It is used to measure durations or intervals in various contexts such as physics, chemistry, and everyday life.

ss2.desc: "ss2" is a unit of time measurement equal to half of a second. It is commonly used in measuring short durations, especially in sports and photography.

ss4.desc: "ss4" is a time unit representing one-fourth of a second. It is commonly used in measuring short durations, especially in sports and photography.

ss8.desc: "ss8" is a unit of time measurement, denoting one-eighth of a second. It is commonly used in measuring short durations, especially in sports and photography.

ss15.desc: "ss15" is a measure of time equal to one-fifteenth of a second. It is commonly used in measuring short durations, especially in sports and photography.

ss30.desc: "ss30" is a time unit equivalent to one-thirtieth of a second. It is commonly used in measuring short durations, especially in sports and photography.

ss60.desc: "ss60" is a time unit equivalent to one-sixtieth of a second. It is commonly used in measuring short durations, such as in photography to measure shutter speed.

ss125.desc: The physical unit "ss125" is a measure of time. It represents 0.008 seconds. It is commonly used in photography to measure shutter speed.

ss250.desc: The physical unit "ss250" is a measure of time. It represents 0.004 seconds. It is commonly used in photography to measure shutter speed.

ss500.desc: The "ss500" is a unit of time measuring 0.002 seconds..

ss1000.desc: The "ss1000" is a time unit equivalent to 0.001 seconds, commonly used in measuring short durations.

ms.desc: "ms" stands for millisecond, a unit of time equal to one thousandth of a second. It is commonly used in measuring short intervals, such as in computing or scientific experiments.

mics.desc: "Mics" is a unit of time measurement equal to one millionth of a second, also known as a microsecond. It is commonly used in technical and scientific fields for precise timing.

ns.desc: A nanosecond (ns) is a unit of time equal to one billionth of a second. It is commonly used in various scientific and technological applications due to its extremely short duration.

wk.desc: The physical unit "wk" stands for week and is commonly used to measure time, particularly in work schedules or project timelines. It is equivalent to 7 days and is a common unit in the field of labor and scheduling.

fortnight.desc: A fortnight is a unit of time equal to two weeks or 14 days. It is commonly used in labor scheduling and project timelines.

yr.desc: "yr" is a unit of time used to measure periods of approximately 365 days or the time it takes for the Earth to orbit the Sun. It is commonly known as a year in everyday language.

mo.desc: The unit "mo" is a commonly used abbreviation for month. It is used to measure time, typically consisting of 30 or 31 days in a calendar month.

bimo.desc: A "bimo" is a unit of time equivalent to two months, often used in business or project planning. It is also known as bi-month.

qrtr.desc: A "qrtr" is a shorthand term for a quarter, typically used in the context of time. It represents 1/4 of an year, often associated with dividing tasks or schedules into smaller increments.

halfyr.desc: A "halfyr" is a time unit equivalent to half of a year, typically used in financial reporting or project timelines. It represents a duration of six months.

dsr.desc: The "dsr" is a unit of time used in the context of half-life or labor, representing a sidereal day. It is commonly denoted as "dsr".

hsr.desc: The "hsr" is a unit of time, equivalent to a sidereal hour. (review pending)

minsr.desc: "Minsr" is a unit of time used in astronomy, representing a sidereal minute. It is commonly used to measure half-lives of celestial bodies or duration of labor tasks.

prahar.desc: "Prahar" is a time unit used in Indian culture, equivalent to three hours. It is commonly used to divide the day into segments for various activities and routines.

shake.desc: A shake is a unit of time equal to ten nanoseconds. It is commonly used in scientific fields such as nuclear physics to measure extremely short time intervals.

ssr.desc: The "ssr" is a unit of time used in astronomy, known as the sidereal second. It is a measure of time based on the rotation of the Earth relative to distant stars.

yrsr.desc: The physical unit "yrsr" is a measurement of time, specifically a sidereal year. It is used to track the orbital period of a celestial body relative to the fixed stars.

yrtp.desc: The "yrtp" is a unit of time representing the tropical year, the time it takes for the Earth to complete one orbit around the Sun relative to the vernal equinox.

thyr.desc: A "thyr" is a time unit equivalent to a thousand years. It is commonly used in the fields of geology, archaeology, and astronomy to describe long periods of time.

lcyr.desc: The physical unit "lcyr" or "lac year" is a time measurement used in the context of half-life calculations in nuclear physics. It represents the decay of a radioactive substance over a period equivalent to 1.25 years.

mnyr.desc: The "mnyr" is a unit of time equal to one million years. It is commonly used in geology and astronomy to describe long periods of time in a more manageable scale.

cryr.desc: The physical unit "cryr" is a measurement of time equivalent to one hundred million years and is commonly used in the field of geology and astronomy for long-term calculations.

bnyr.desc: A "bnyr" is a unit of time equal to one billion years. It is commonly used in scientific contexts to measure long durations, such as geological processes or astronomical events.

quectosec.desc: A quectosec, short for quectosecond, is a unit of time equivalent to one thousandth of a second. It is commonly used in scientific and technical fields for precise measurements and calculations.

rontosec.desc: A rontosec, also known as a rontosecond, is a unit of time used to measure half-life. (review pending)

yottasec.desc: A yottasecond (yottasec) is a unit of time equal to 10^24 seconds. It is an extremely large measurement used in scientific calculations involving vast amounts of time such as the age of the universe or the lifespan of stars.

zettasec.desc: A zettasecond (zettasec) is a unit of time equal to 10^21 seconds. It is used in scientific calculations and is an extremely large unit of time.

exasec.desc: Exasec, short for exasecond, is a unit of time, representing one quintillion seconds. It is commonly used in scientific research and high-performance computing.

petasec.desc: A petasec, also known as a petasecond, is a unit of time equal to 10^15 seconds. It is used to measure extremely long periods of time, often in scientific and astronomical contexts.

terasec.desc: A terasec, also known as a terasecond, is a unit of time equal to one trillion seconds. It is commonly used in scientific and technological contexts for measuring long durations.

gigasec.desc: A gigasec, also known as a gigasecond, is a unit of time equal to one billion seconds. It is commonly used in scientific and technological applications for measuring long durations.

megasec.desc: A megasec is a unit of time equal to one million seconds, commonly used in scientific and technical fields for measuring long durations.

kilosec.desc: A kilosec is a unit of time equivalent to 1,000 seconds. It is commonly used in scientific and technical contexts to measure short periods of time.

hectosec.desc: A hectosec, also known as a hectosecond, is a unit of time equal to 100 seconds. It is commonly used in scientific and technical contexts for precise measurements of time intervals.

decasec.desc: A decasec, also known as a decasecond, is a unit of time equal to 10 seconds. It is commonly used in scientific measurements and calculations.

decisec.desc: A decisec, also known as a decisecond, is a unit of time equal to one-tenth of a second. It is commonly used in scientific and technical contexts for precise measurements.

centisec.desc: A centisec is a unit of time equal to one hundredth of a second. It is commonly used in scientific measurements and calculations involving short durations.

millisec.desc: A millisec is a unit of time equal to one thousandth of a second. It is commonly used in scientific and engineering applications to measure short time intervals.

microsec.desc: A microsecond (µs) is a unit of time equal to one millionth of a second. It is commonly used in electronics, telecommunications, and scientific research.

nanosec.desc: A nanosecond, abbreviated as "nanosec", is a unit of time equal to one billionth of a second. It is commonly used in scientific and technological fields for precise measurements and calculations.

picosec.desc: A picosecond (picosec) is a unit of time equal to one trillionth of a second, commonly used in scientific and technological fields for precise measurements and calculations.

femtosec.desc: A femtosecond (femtosec) is a unit of time equal to one quadrillionth of a second. It is commonly used in the study of ultrafast processes in physics and chemistry.

attosec.desc: An attosecond is a unit of time equal to one quintillionth of a second, used in scientific research to measure extremely short time intervals in the realm of atomic and molecular interactions.

zeptosec.desc: A zeptosecond (zeptosec) is a unit of time equal to 10^-21 seconds. It is used in the study of extremely short time intervals, such as nuclear processes.

yoctosec.desc: A yoctosecond (yoctosec) is a unit of time equal to one septillionth of a second. It is used in scientific calculations, particularly in the study of particle decay and nuclear reactions.
